findings.text: _update_git_answer_store re-implements the atomic JSON replacement and the exclusive flock that reckon/_store.py already owns (write_json_atomically at :619, _serialized_path_lock at :394), which reckon/crew/gate_watch.py:156 and reckon/crew/recovery_memo.py:197 already use for a lock-guarded store write and a persisted derivation cache; the crew home now carries two lock disciplines (a .lock file beside the store here, locks/<namespace>/<sha>.lock there) and the store bypasses the owner's fsync and mode handling.

§44 states 'the store is bounded: a write drops entries no live pointer names', but _bound_git_answer_store only consults the live pointers once max(len(commits), len(counts)) exceeds _GIT_ANSWER_STORE_WORKTREES (256), so below the ceiling it retains entries for every tree that still exists on disk whatever the live pointers name — bounded, but not by the rule the plan states.

assert subject_module._resolve_commit(worktree, head) == head compares the call against the same head the test just passed in, so a store that stored and returned its own candidate would satisfy it; the resolve half of the store is therefore never checked against an independent value (the same shape recurs at :344). A full revision genuinely resolves to itself, so no independent source exists, but the 'the store answers what git answers' claim holds only for the count at :298.

_stored_commit_answer returns a stored sha without establishing that tree still holds that object; _bound_git_answer_store prunes only trees that are no longer directories, so a worktree path removed and reused by a different repository keeps its entries and _resolve_commit would report a commit the new tree does not have — the case reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:123-125's docstring says cannot happen. Callers such as reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:950 treat a non-empty answer as 'this commit exists here'.
